the use of ACTH and corticosteroids is beneficial in infantile epileptic syndromes, but the final seizure outcome is poor in symptomatic cases.

the use of ACTH and corticosteroids in the treatment of infantile epileptics encephalopathes, especially in symptomatic West syndrome, is beneficial in controlling spasms but has no significant influence on long-term outcome.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the diagnosis of infantile epileptiform encephalopathy is a clinical diagnosis, but it is imperative that the clinician should be aware of the various syndromes and the clinical and electroencephalographic features that help in the diagnosis.
early identification and intervention in infantile epileptic syndromes is essential to achieve a better outcome in terms of seizure control, developmental outcome and quality of life.
